content_voiceover: This table summarizes the first choice bispecific antibody regimens for multiply relapsed or refractory myeloma. Teclistamab, studied in the MajesTEC-1 trial, uses step up dosing, point zero six milligrams per kilogram on day one, point three milligrams per kilogram on day four, spaced two to seven days apart, followed by the standard weekly dose of one point five milligrams per kilogram starting two to seven days after the final step up dose. It's FDA approved for fifth line or later therapy and gained Taiwan FDA approval, and as of May first, twenty twenty five, it's now covered by national health insurance. Elranatamab, from the MagnetisMM-3 trial, is given subcutaneously with step up dosing of twelve milligrams per kilogram on day one and thirty two milligrams per kilogram on day four, at least two days apart, then a standard dose of seventy six milligrams weekly starting day eight for twenty four weeks, after which responders can switch to dosing every two weeks. It also became health insurance covered as of May first, twenty twenty five. Talquetamab, from the MonumenTAL-1 trial, offers weekly or every two week subcutaneous dosing, point four milligrams per kilogram weekly or point eight milligrams per kilogram every two weeks, each with its own step up schedule. It's FDA approved for fifth line therapy and has Taiwan FDA approval, though it isn't yet covered by national health insurance.
keypoints: Teclistamab, elranatamab, and talquetamab use step-up dosing to reduce cytokine release syndrome
All three are FDA approved for fifth line or later relapsed refractory myeloma
Teclistamab and elranatamab gained Taiwan health insurance coverage May 2025
Talquetamab has Taiwan FDA approval but is not yet reimbursed
keypoint_voiceover: Key point here, all three T cell redirecting bispecifics, teclistamab, elranatamab, and talquetamab, use step up dosing to mitigate cytokine release syndrome, and while all are FDA approved for late line disease, only teclistamab and elranatamab currently have Taiwan health insurance coverage.
